stories.headline: Jensen Huang says he'd return as Nvidia CEO, but the board isn't considering it
points: First statement since resigning last week: says he would be honoured to return if the board judged it in shareholders' interest, and takes responsibility for his mistakes
Three sources told Reuters the board is not weighing reinstatement; Nvidia has hired Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent CEO
Board created a national security and export control committee; Huang testifies to House committees behind closed doors on 1 December
Nvidia has lost about US$2T (35%) of its value since its October peak and now sits behind Apple and Microsoft

stories.headline: US rule targets Chinese firms renting US AI chips through the cloud
points: New Commerce Department rule restricts remote access to advanced US AI chips by Chinese companies, closing the cloud rental workaround
Nvidia warned customers they could face legal exposure under the rule
Commerce and DOJ also confirmed a criminal probe into Singapore's Megaspeed over possible diversion of restricted Nvidia chips

stories.headline: Optimizely supply-chain attack planted card skimmers on 178 sites, including Australian brands
points: Attackers abused a flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation's signup flow to inject JavaScript into customers' sites
Australian victims include Vodafone, TPG Telecom, HSBC Australia, Rest Super, Betashares and Levi's Australia
Payload skimmed card details from forms, swapped crypto wallet addresses and pushed unpatched iPhones to exploit kits
Live from 3:21pm AEDT Monday until most scripts were cleaned by 8:10am AEDT Tuesday

stories.headline: Anthropic guides IPO to the top of its US$70 to $78 range or above
points: Top of range values Anthropic at about US$1.4T fully diluted and raises up to US$64.4B on Nasdaq under ticker ANT
Filing shows Amazon and Google will hold about 15% and 14% of the stock after listing
Seven chip and cloud suppliers, including Nvidia, Google and Microsoft, are buying US$26B of non-voting shares at the IPO price

stories.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in ChatGPT, Codex and the API
points: Astra is the flagship for hard projects; OpenAI says it is better at changing and testing existing codebases in Codex
Sol is the cheaper everyday model and scored within half a point of Astra on FrontierCode 2.0 at about a fifth of the cost
Astra API pricing is 20% lower than GPT-6 Astra; Sol keeps GPT-6.1 pricing
New Ultrafast mode generates up to 4.5x faster on Pro plans

stories.headline: Microsoft launches its own coding and security models at Ignite
points: MAI Code 2 is pitched as nearly matching rival coding models at a fraction of the cost
A cyber security model goes to a limited set of customers to deal with the surge in AI-found vulnerabilities
Image generation and transcription models also released; a direct move to reduce reliance on OpenAI and Anthropic

stories.headline: Google will keep history-off Gemini chats for two months instead of 72 hours
points: Applies to temporary chats and chats with history turned off; rolling out globally over the coming weeks
Google cites safety and security; it says temporary chats still aren't used for training
Chat history and AI training are now separate settings, so you can keep history without allowing training
For comparison, ChatGPT and Claude keep temporary chats for up to 30 days

stories.headline: macOS 27.3 tightens Full Disk Access as AI agents ask for more control
points: Device Control and Data Access split into System & App Protection Override and Accessibility, making clear the first bypasses built-in protections
Apps can be set to ask permission every time, limiting an agent's standing access; a new indicator shows when one app controls another
Backup and assistive apps can request entitlements to keep existing Full Disk Access behaviour

stories.headline: ANZ moved a 1.7PB Hadoop platform to AWS in six months using AI agents
points: On-prem Cloudera Hadoop to Amazon EMR: 300 million files, 142,000 tables and 4,500 automated workflows, mostly lift-and-shift
Expected to take 18 months; ANZ says coding and troubleshooting agents cut effort by about 35% and halved defects and rework
Sensitive data was tokenised before the move; tokenisation running costs fell from over US$10k a day to under US$3k a month

stories.headline: Firaxis cuts about a third of its staff
points: Take-Two's Civilization and XCOM studio is reportedly laying off roughly a third of employees
The studio head is also leaving

read.title: World's largest brands infected with malware via Optimizely
read.why: Scott Helme's 15-minute teardown of the attack: timeline, payload behaviour, and how a Content Security Policy would have caught it.
